topic: Khums year of someone with an occupation
states: The year of anyone with an occupation (trader, employee, farmer, teacher, worker…) ends one year after starting work; at that point khums is due on everything existing and not spent on needs, even income of the previous day. No separate year per profit (except several occupations, 565).

topic: Who counts as having an occupation
states: Someone whose earned income over the year is a significant amount relative to yearly expenses (examples: 5% is not, 25% is); when doubtful, treated as not having an occupation and may keep a separate year per income.
issues: The 5% and 25% figures are examples, not thresholds: the person's status is asked as a confirmation.

topic: Several different occupations
states: Different kinds of occupation with separate accounts may each have their own year if each yields a significant income; a minor second occupation follows the main one's year.
issues: Separate yearly cycles need date capability.

topic: New activity of the same kind
states: A second activity of the same kind (another shop, other crops) cannot have its own year.

topic: Seasonal earners
states: Seasonal earners whose yearly earned income is significant count as having an occupation: one year for all income.

topic: Income from capital given to others or rented property
states: A significant income from mudaraba, bank investment under Islamic contracts, or renting property makes the person count as having an occupation.

topic: Incidental income of someone with an occupation
states: No separate year for incidental income (a one-off sale, gifts).

topic: Incidental income with two yearly cycles
states: May add it to either cycle, never a separate one.

topic: Exact end of the khums year
states: The year ends at the same hour work began, one year later; remaining income may not be used after that moment.
issues: The calculator works by date; the hour is noted for the person.

topic: No known start date
states: Someone with an occupation and no known start who settles with a jurist or his agent and pays: the payment time becomes the khums year point.

workflows.firstTime: named (year point set at first payment)

issues: Settlement itself is with a jurist: recorded, not computed.

topic: Khums year without an occupation
states: People without an occupation (supported by state or others, incidental income) pay on what exceeds the year's expenses one year after owning each income; may keep a separate year per income.
issues: Per-income yearly cycles need date capability.

topic: Start of each income's year
states: For people without an occupation, each income's year starts when it is owned, not when it is converted (e.g. into goods).

topic: End of each income's year
states: Once a year passes from owning that income, it may not be used for needs until khums is paid.

topic: Retiring or stopping work mid-year
states: Keeps the occupation rules until that year ends; afterwards, if without work, the rules for people without an occupation apply.

topic: Calendar of the khums year
states: Solar, lunar or Gregorian year may be used.

topic: Changing the khums year
states: Moving it later: assess and pay at the old date, then again at the new date for the months between. Moving it earlier: assess and pay at the new date. Same with a settlement taking khums as a debt.
issues: A transitional short year needs date capability.

topic: Lunar to solar year
states: Allowed before the lunar year ends; once ended, khums is due and cannot wait for the solar date, but the new year may be solar.

topic: Doubt whether the year has passed
states: May assume the year has not passed (e.g. lost records); but someone at fault (no accounts, negligence) settles with a jurist proportionate to probability, by obligatory precaution.
issues: Fault and probability are judged with a jurist: stop and refer.

topic: Death during the year
states: Spending until death is exempt; khums on the rest is due immediately; funeral costs are not deducted. Heirs need not pay for one who deliberately never paid and left no will.
issues: The calculator assesses living persons.

topic: Paying during the year
states: May pay when income arrives or delay to year end; if it will certainly remain unneeded, pay at once by obligatory precaution.

topic: Earned and unearned income
states: Earned income includes trade, industry, farming, employment and salaries, labour, renting out property, hunting, gathering free things. Unearned includes gifts, prizes, rewards and bequests. Both owe khums if not spent on the year's needs.

topic: Receiving a gift already taxed or inherited
states: Such a gift is the recipient's income of the year; khums if it remains unspent at year end.

topic: Two kinds of mu'nah
states: Khums falls on income after deducting the year's mu'nah: costs of earning income, and the year's personal and family expenses.

topic: Costs of earning income
states: All spending to earn income with nothing received in return (wages of staff, porters, brokers, shop rent, taxes…) is deducted; if paid from a loan, the debt is deducted. Wear on taxed or inherited tools of trade counts too (example: a car bought from taxed money losing value through rental use).
issues: Depreciation of tools needs start and year-end values (valuation capability).

topic: The year's personal and family expenses: three groups and five conditions
states: Consumables; durable items used for their benefit (home, furniture, clothes, women's gold jewellery, computer, books, vehicle…); running costs (gifts, charity, guests, pilgrimage or leisure travel, vows and kaffarah, repaying debts for family expenses, children's wedding or education, medical care, diyah paid, compensation paid). Exempt only if: (1) paid from the year's income, not income whose year passed unpaid; (2) customary and within status; (3) not extravagant or unlawful; (4) for consumables and durables, customarily needed during the year; (5) consumed, used, or spent before year end.
issues: Status, extravagance and customary need are the person's own determinations (asked as confirmations).

topic: Unlawful or extravagant spending
states: Spending that is unlawful or extravagant owes khums; spending beyond status owes khums on the excess; even meritorious spending abnormal for the person owes khums on the excess by obligatory precaution.
issues: The excess beyond status is not computable by the calculator: asked or stopped.

topic: Criterion of status
states: Status is set by custom (family, education, job, marital status, children, income, social standing, place and time), within the limits of no extravagance and nothing unlawful; the person judges the facts.
issues: Supports asking the person to confirm 'within status'.

topic: Doubt whether an item is within status
states: When doubting whether an item is within status, khums on the doubtful amount is due; if previously within status and doubt arises later, it is treated as within status.
issues: The doubtful amount is the person's own figure.

topic: Doubt whether an item was used
states: At year end, doubt whether an item bought or gifted was used means khums is due, unless the item's mere existence counts as mu'nah (605, 612, 614).

topic: Left-over consumables
states: Worthless remains owe nothing; valuable remains owe nothing if the smallest available size was bought, otherwise they owe khums; same for gifts.

topic: Valuation of unused items at year end
states: Left-over consumables and unused items bought from the year's income are valued at the year-end price (recommended precaution: purchase price if it fell).
issues: Needs year-end value input (valuation capability).

topic: Unused items that were needed
states: Items not used before year end owe khums even if needed, except: buying ahead is customary for one's status, or buying later when needed would be impossible or cause unusual hardship.
exceptions: Later purchase impossible or very hard
issues: Both exceptions are the person's own determinations.

topic: Sets sold only together
states: If part of a needed set (books, dishes) is used during the year, the rest is exempt.

topic: Items given to family to use without ownership
states: Exempt if customary for the person's status (e.g. jewellery for a wife's use, a book for a child).

topic: Items for both personal and work use
states: Exempt if personal use is substantial; if the item is customarily a work item, khums on the price difference above a personal-use equivalent; if personal use is minor, all is liable.
issues: Price of a personal-use equivalent is the person's own figure.

topic: Trousseau and marriage savings
states: Gradual trousseau purchases within status and custom are exempt; bought after the year passed, or gradually without need, they owe khums. Same for a son's future household items. Money set aside or saved for a trousseau, household items or wedding costs owes khums at year end even if the conditions hold.
issues: Savings for marriage: liable.

topic: Trousseau used for other needs
states: Exempt trousseau later used for other needs stays exempt; if sold, the rules of selling mu'nah apply (632–633).

topic: Building a home gradually; home savings
states: Materials and land for a home built over years owe khums at each year end, unless gradual building is the only and customary way for the person and not doing so is a shortfall in status; money saved for a future home owes khums even then.
issues: The 'only way and customary' condition is the person's determination.

topic: Home rented out to pay its price
states: A home bought within status and rented out to pay off its price owes khums at year end after deducting its debt, unless that is the only customary way to own a home.

topic: First home rented out, a larger second home bought
states: The first home owes nothing. The second: liable if the first was sufficient; liable up to the first home's current value if the first was too small; exempt if the move was for other reasons (location, neighbours, distance to work).
issues: Needs the first home's current value; reason for moving is the person's own answer.

topic: State subsidies paid by bank transfer (Shetab)
states: Subsidies paid by interbank transfer into a household head's account are not liable until withdrawn in cash; once withdrawn and owned they are income of that year, liable if unspent at year end.
issues: Specific to Iran's Shetab network: other payment routes stop for review.

topic: Subsidies paid into an investment account
states: If the person appointed the bank as agent for Islamic investment and it invested the funds during the year, the invested sum is income of the year, treated as business capital (640).

topic: Insurance premiums and payouts
states: Premiums paid from the year's income for customary insurance within status are exempt; payouts received by Shetab transfer follow the subsidy rule (620–621); death payouts to named beneficiaries are not inheritance.
issues: Payouts by other routes stop for review.

topic: Investment-type insurance
states: Follows the rules of bank investment (676–677); on death, principal and profit to that date are part of the estate.

topic: Pension fund contributions and pension payments
states: A pension contract (share of monthly salary paid to a fund; fund pays bonus or pension by transfer) follows the insurance rule (624).
issues: Already encoded in the 0.10.0 packs (sis-620); Shetab-only route.

topic: Selling an item of mu'nah after its first year
states: A rise in value of items in use is not liable; if sold after the first year, the original price is exempt; the rise is exempt if received without exchange (gift), but if bought from the year's income it is income of the year of sale.
issues: Needs purchase price and sale price.

topic: Selling an item of mu'nah within its first year
states: If sold within the first year and the price stays unspent at year end: original price liable by obligatory precaution; the rise liable (fatwa if bought, obligatory precaution if gifted).

topic: Need for an item ending
states: If need ends after the first year, no khums; if it ends within the first year, khums by precaution; seasonal items set aside are not liable.

topic: Spending from income while having taxed property
states: May spend the year's income on needs instead of taxed or inherited property; but if an existing taxed or inherited item already meets the need (e.g. an inherited house that suffices), buying another from income is not mu'nah.

topic: Former mu'nah sold to buy a shop
states: A home or car used as mu'nah and sold (same price or less) after its year to buy a shop: the shop owes nothing, and a new home or car may be bought from income.

topic: Taxed money mixed with income
states: Intention has no effect on withdrawals from a mixed fund: jointly owned shares are drawn proportionally; otherwise drawn first from the year's income.
issues: Needs tracking of taxed vs untaxed balances.

topic: Taxed money and income owed by another (e.g. bank)
states: When collecting part of a debt, both sides must intend which share it is; for state or semi-state banks the account holder's intention suffices; otherwise proportional.

topic: Business capital: basic and expansion
states: Basic capital (the minimum needed to live within status) bought from the year's income is not mu'nah and owes khums, unless paying it, even by settlement and instalments over years, would make life within status impossible or unbearably hard or force unsuitable work; then not required (but any part that can be paid is due). Expansion capital owes khums.
issues: Hardship is the person's own determination: asked, never judged.

topic: Shops, premises and tools
states: The capital rule (640) applies to shops, factories, tools, transport vehicles, machines.

topic: Rise in value of taxed trading goods
states: If taxed or inherited property held for trade rises and can be sold, the market rise owes khums at year end even if unsold.
issues: Needs year-end market value (valuation capability).

topic: Rise in value of taxed non-trading property
states: Received without exchange (inheritance): the rise is never liable, even after sale. Bought: not liable until sold; on sale, the purchase price is exempt and the rise is income of the year of sale. Gifted property taxed from itself: rise exempt; taxed from other money: four-fifths as unexchanged, one-fifth as exchanged.
issues: Needs acquisition route, purchase price and sale price.

topic: Rise caused by inflation
states: Where a rise would be liable, liability for a rise caused by inflation is problematic: obligatory precaution, where the real gain is not clear after the currency's loss of value; the person may refer to the next most learned mujtahid who holds otherwise. The part above inflation is a gain.
issues: Inflation adjustment needs a scholar: stop and refer.

topic: Trading goods bought on credit
states: A sellable rise on goods bought on credit and still unpaid is income of the year (purchase price exempt while unpaid); inflationary rises as in 647; goods bought from the year's income owe khums at current value even if the rise is inflation.

topic: Taxed money converted to gold or land to keep its value
states: Not trade: yearly rises owe nothing; on sale, the rise is income of the year of sale (inflation part as in 647).

topic: Rise then fall in the same year
states: No khums on a rise that falls back within the year (trade and non-trade).

topic: Rise at year end, fall next year
states: Trade goods held for a higher price: khums on the year-end rise by obligatory precaution. Non-trade goods stored for later use: current value suffices.

topic: Base for later rises after paying khums
states: After paying khums on an item's year-end value, later rises are measured above that taxed value, not the purchase price.
issues: Needs the taxed value recorded per item (carry-over).

topic: Growth of taxed property
states: Separate or near-separate growth (fruit, offspring, milk, wool) of non-mu'nah taxed or inherited property owes khums at year end; attached growth that counts as increase (animals kept for meat) too.
issues: Agricultural and livestock valuation is outside the inputs.

topic: Livestock products and weight gain
states: Products, offspring and customary weight gain left over at year end owe khums; sale proceeds unspent at year end too.

topic: Gold or currency dealers: measuring profit
states: A dealer whose capital is gold or currency may measure profit and loss either in local currency, or in the gold weight/coin count or currency units themselves (then a price rise is not profit and a fall is not loss). Only for gold and currency capital; first switch requires paying khums at local-currency value.
conditions: Business capital of gold or currency
issues: Choice of measure is the person's; the calculator does not offer it yet.

topic: Other traders measuring in gold or foreign currency
states: A trader may convert capital to gold or a foreign currency and measure profit in it, after first paying khums at local-currency value.

topic: Valuing trading stock at year end
states: Stock may be valued as a whole at the price it would fetch without extra selling costs or waiting (like a clearance price), not so low as to be a loss; experts may be consulted (the more expert preferred; average of equals).
issues: The person enters the year-end stock value; the calculator never estimates it.

topic: Hire for work spanning years
states: Wages for work done in the contract year are that year's income; the rest belongs to later years.
issues: Needs a split of the wage per year (dates).

topic: Selling a garden's produce for several years
states: The whole price is income of the year of sale; unspent amount minus the garden's loss of value is liable.

topic: Multi-year rent received
states: Rent for several years is income of the contract year (even instalments later); unspent rent minus the property's loss of value is liable immediately.
issues: Needs the property's loss of value (user figure).

topic: Amount set aside for the property's loss of value
states: If unspent, each year's share becomes income of that year, unless it equals that year's wear (cost of earning).

topic: Rent paid in advance for a home
states: Rent prepaid from the year's income: khums on the remaining months' benefit at year end, unless prepaying was the only way to rent a home within status.

topic: Bank investment deposits (wakala)
states: Principal deposited from the year's income in an Islamic agency investment account follows business capital (640).

topic: Profit of bank investment accounts
states: Definite profit credited is income of that year; provisional 'on account' payments, or payments with doubtful profit that cannot be checked, are not yet liable.
issues: Whether profit is definite or on account is the person's answer.

topic: Bank profit without agency
states: Not liable until withdrawn; withdrawn from a state or joint bank in Muslim countries it is property of unknown owner: half as charity to devout poor Shia, the other half becomes income.
issues: Unknown-owner property: stop and refer.

topic: Companies paying khums for shareholders
states: With shareholders' permission, managers may pay khums on shares or profits; otherwise each shareholder pays. Mosques and similar legal persons owe none.

topic: Shares bought with taxed money to trade
states: A sellable rise is income even if unsold; liable if unspent at year end.
issues: Needs year-end market value.

topic: Shares bought with taxed money not to trade
states: Rise not liable until sold; on sale, the rise is income of that year.

topic: Shares bought from the year's income
states: Not mu'nah: khums at year-end value, except the capital exception (640).
issues: Needs year-end value.

topic: Share dividends
states: Received or credited dividends above mu'nah owe khums; profit earned but payable after the year may be taxed now at current value or when received; retained earnings kept by the company owe khums; 'on account' payments without profit are not liable.

topic: Trading loss offset within the year
states: Losses on taxed trading capital are offset by profit of the same year, before or after the loss (example given).

topic: Loss or damage during the year
states: Taxed stock lost by theft, fire, earthquake, and taxed tools worn through work, are deducted from that year's income; loss of non-business taxed property (home, personal car) is not.

topic: Losses of someone without an occupation
states: Loss of personal taxed property is not deducted from income.

topic: Compensation owed for damaged taxed property
states: The claim replacing taxed or inherited property owes no khums.

topic: Loss in a year without profit
states: Cannot be offset against next year's profit; the taxed base simply falls.

workflows.missedYear: named across years (no carry-forward of losses)

topic: Doubt which year income belongs to
states: If unsure whether later income belongs to the loss year, the loss cannot be offset from it.

topic: Income lost during the year
states: Income lost by flood, earthquake or theft owes no khums.

topic: Taxed money spent on needs (someone with an occupation)
states: The same amount may be deducted from that year's income, whether income came before or after; not for durable items whose substance remains (e.g. a taxed carpet).

topic: Taxed money spent on needs (no occupation)
states: Deductible only from income already owned (and within its year) at the time of spending, not from later income.
issues: Needs dates of income and spending.

topic: Taxed consumables used after a price rise
states: Replacement from the year's income is at purchase price, not the higher price at use (obligatory precaution).

topic: Fungible taxed consumables used next year
states: Fungible goods taxed last year and used this year may be replaced by their like from this year's income (value on the khums day).

topic: Taxed money spent on business costs
states: Deductible from that year's income, before or after.

topic: Taxed money spent in a year without income
states: Cannot be deducted from the next year's income.

topic: Livestock used or sold for needs
states: Shortfall in taxed herd may be made up from that year's offspring and products; applies to other occupations.

topic: Occupations whose income comes in later years
states: Taxed money spent on preparing income for later years (mining, land preparation, orchards) and wear on taxed tools for next year's income may be deducted from those later years' income; household spending before income may not.

workflows.missedYear: named across years (deduction in later years)

issues: Needs carry-over of deferred costs.

topic: Repaying a needs debt with taxed money later
states: Someone with an occupation who paid khums despite a needs debt (debt rule not met) may deduct later repayments made with taxed money from the year of repayment; without an occupation, only from income existing when repaying.
issues: Needs carry-over of debt repayments.

topic: Exempted amount spent the next year while the debt remains
states: If income was exempted because of a needs debt and is spent on needs next year while the debt is still unpaid, it may be replaced from that year's income (example: home debt).
issues: Needs carry-over of exempted amounts.

topic: Several lines of business (Jami' wording of 1790)
states: Lines united in accounts offset profit and loss; different kinds of business, or same kind with separate accounts: no offset, by obligatory precaution.
issues: Already encoded in the 0.10.0 packs (sis-1790).

topic: Salary spent on a second business with its own year
states: Salary spent on the trading business's costs is taxed at the salary's year end, then deductible from the trading income of that business's year.
issues: Two yearly cycles: needs date capability.

topic: Repaying debt is mu'nah
states: Income spent before year end on repaying a debt is exempt, whether the debt arose this year or earlier, and whether or not it could have been repaid before.

topic: Debt deduction rule (someone with an occupation)
states: An unpaid debt at year end does not reduce khums, unless: (a) it is for mu'nah (living or business); (b) for one-off mu'nah, the need and the exempted income both fall in the current khums year; for lasting mu'nah (home, vehicle, furniture), an unpaid debt may be deducted from later years' income where that year's income was insufficient; (c) for one-off mu'nah, it arose after starting work. Example: unpaid mahr of a marriage this year exempts that much of this year's surplus.
issues: Deduction from later years for lasting mu'nah needs carry-over.

topic: Debt deduction rule (no occupation)
states: Same, but: the exempted income must exist (even as a receivable) when the need arose, within twelve months of that income; lasting mu'nah may be deducted from later income.
conditions: Income existed at the time of the need
issues: Needs dates of income and of the need.

topic: Loan date vs date of spending
states: For someone without an occupation, the debt counts against income existing when the borrowed money is spent on the need, even if that income arose after the borrowing.

topic: Notes on the debt rule
states: Applies to debts with or without a term, lump or instalments; regardless of intention to repay from that income; the exempt income may be money, goods, property; it applies automatically (extra khums paid by mistake is not khums unless a jurist allows counting it for future years).

topic: Exempted income while the debt stays unpaid
states: Exempted income stays exempt as long as the debt is unpaid, even for years; if it is trading stock, its later price rises follow the trade-goods rules.
issues: Needs carry-over of exempted amounts.

topic: Debts of occupations with later income
states: Debts for business costs before income are deducted from the later years' income they produce; debts for one-off living needs are not (though they may be repaid from later income during its year); debts for lasting needs may be.

topic: Debt in gold or foreign currency
states: If gold or currency borrowed and sold for needs has risen by year end, the year-end value may be deducted under the debt rule.
issues: Needs year-end value of the gold or currency owed.

topic: Repaying an exempting debt in later years
states: Repaid with the exempted money: nothing due. Repaid from new income: the exempted money (if still there) becomes new income. Repaid with taxed money: the exempted money counts as taxed. Repaid with a new loan: as if unpaid. Partial repayment applies pro rata.
issues: Needs carry-over of exempted amounts and repayments.

topic: Loan for a non-mu'nah item repaid from the year's income
states: Khums on the item at its current value at year end, unless it perished or became mu'nah during the year.
issues: Needs current value.

topic: Non-mu'nah item on loan, nothing repaid by year end
states: Not liable that year; when repaid from new income, the item (or the repaid proportion) becomes new income, liable at current value if it remains.
issues: Needs carry-over of repaid proportions.

topic: Home within status bought on credit
states: Repayments of a home lived in before year end are mu'nah (this year or later); same for other mu'nah bought on credit.

topic: Receivables at year end
states: Collectable receivables that are income owe khums even if not demanded. If not collectable now: either pay when collected (as last year's income, immediately), or pay now on their present cash value (excess later is new income). Applies to loans, credit sale profits, wages.
issues: Present cash value is the person's own figure; the choice is the person's.

topic: Receivables that are not income
states: A loan of taxed money owes nothing when repaid; lending income whose year has passed: khums is due on it at once.

topic: Deposit paid for renting a home or shop (rahn)
states: Paid from the year's income, it is a receivable like 715 once the year passes; the receiving owner owes nothing on it.

topic: Family loan circles
states: On receiving the loan, khums is due at once on the part repaying one's earlier contributions whose year passed; the rest is a loan.

topic: Using property after khums became due
states: Not allowed until paid, even if intending to pay or setting it aside, unless a jurist permits or a settlement is made; taking it as a debt without a jurist makes one liable if lost.

topic: Delaying payment with a jurist's permission
states: Permission is conditional on: inability or great hardship in paying now; if value falls, khums at year-end value, if it rises, at payment-time value; liability if lost; one-fifth of benefits during the delay; one-fifth of the customary rent for the delay if rentable. A settlement fixes the amount instead.

workflows.missedYear: named (delayed dues: value at payment time if risen)

issues: Values at year end and at payment, and rent of the delay period, are inputs; the permission itself is with a jurist.

topic: Buying with the very untaxed money
states: Valid if the seller is a Twelver Shia, who may use all the money.

topic: Buying on credit and paying with untaxed money
states: Valid; the khums moves to the buyer's liability as a debt to the khums recipients.

topic: Forgiving a loan
states: Before year end: exempt if forgiving is within status; after year end: valid for a Twelver Shia debtor, but the lender owes khums on it.

topic: Unpaid item that rose in value and was sold the next year
states: Pay the fifth of the original, all profit earned on the fifth's share, and a fifth of the profit on one's own share; by obligatory precaution paying a fifth of what exists at the new year end is not enough (worked example).
issues: Needs year-end value, sale price and the sale year's end (carry-over).

topic: Unpaid trees or seed that grew
states: Pay the fifth of the original, its growth, and a fifth of one's own share's growth; obligatory precaution against paying only on the final value.
issues: Agricultural growth valuation is outside the inputs.

topic: Unpaid rentable property: rent for the delay
states: For rentable property (home, shop, taxi) whose khums is delayed, a fifth of its customary rent for the delay is also due, even if not rented; renting it below market makes one liable for the difference.
issues: Needs customary rent of the delay period (user figure).

topic: Item bought with money whose year passed: purchase price or current value
states: Purchase price suffices when (a) bought with money on which khums was due and unpaid, (b) the price was an unspecified obligation (in the buyer's liability), (c) the item is not trading stock; otherwise (bought from the year's income, specified money, or trading stock) khums at current value.
issues: Needs purchase price, purchase kind, trading or not, and current value.

topic: Finding the khums year of someone who never kept accounts
states: The year is not chosen: with an occupation it starts the first day of work, then each twelve months; without, twelve months from owning each income. Someone without accounts first finds the year, then pays khums on what remained unspent at the end of each year.
issues: Already encoded in the 0.10.0 packs (sis-736); per-year work needs the missed-year workflow.

topic: Dividing the property of someone who missed years
states: (a) bought from the year's income: mu'nah used that year owes nothing; non-mu'nah (tools, stock, items not in current use) owes khums at current value. (b) bought with taxed or inherited money: nothing, except trade goods' rise. (c) bought with money whose year passed: unspecified price → purchase price suffices, unless trading stock that can sell higher (current value); specified price from a Twelver seller → current value if risen. (d) mixed sources: split and apply each. (e) unknown source: later rulings. Cash and savings (including for marriage) whose year passed owe khums.
issues: Already encoded in the 0.10.0 packs (sis-737); needs purchase kind and current values.

topic: Property spent or lost from income whose year passed
states: For consumables, gifts, charity, guests, pilgrimage, vows, debts for family expenses, children's wedding or education, treatment, compensation, stolen stock, utility bills… paid from income whose year had passed: the person is liable for the khums. If unsure of the amount, the certain amount suffices, unless at fault: then settlement proportionate to probability with a jurist (obligatory precaution).
issues: Already encoded in the 0.10.0 packs (sis-738); fault and probability go to a jurist.

topic: Unknown source or kind of a past purchase
states: If one does not know whether an item was bought from income whose year passed or the year's income, or with a specified or unspecified price, so that liability or purchase-vs-current value is unclear: settlement with a jurist proportionate to probability (obligatory precaution).
issues: The text gives the computation explicitly, but the settlement is made with a jurist (obligatory precaution): the calculator stops and refers. Whether it may show an indicative figure for the jurist is for the scholar to decide.

topic: Settlement worked examples: non-trading item
states: Known unspecified price, unknown income: weighted mix of purchase price and current value by the person's probabilities, times one-fifth. Known specified price: one-fifth of current value. Both unknown: four combinations weighted by probabilities (worked figures given).
issues: The text gives the computation explicitly, but the settlement is made with a jurist (obligatory precaution): the calculator stops and refers. Whether it may show an indicative figure for the jurist is for the scholar to decide.
Already encoded in the 0.10.0 packs as a stop (sis-739).

topic: Unknown source of trading stock
states: Trading stock of unknown source: khums at current value.
issues: Needs current value.

topic: Settlement worked examples: household items
states: Household items of unknown source: settlement by probability; four combinations give exempt / exempt / purchase price / current value (worked figures).
issues: The text gives the computation explicitly, but the settlement is made with a jurist (obligatory precaution): the calculator stops and refers. Whether it may show an indicative figure for the jurist is for the scholar to decide.

topic: Unknown whether an item was used in its year
states: If the item or its replacement exists: settlement by probability (e.g. 30% probable unused → one-fifth of 30% of current value); if it no longer exists, nothing unless at fault.
issues: The text gives the computation explicitly, but the settlement is made with a jurist (obligatory precaution): the calculator stops and refers. Whether it may show an indicative figure for the jurist is for the scholar to decide.

topic: Unknown whether bought with inheritance or the year's income
states: If the item or replacement exists: settlement by probability (e.g. 30% probable from income → one-fifth of 30% of value); if gone, nothing unless at fault.
issues: The text gives the computation explicitly, but the settlement is made with a jurist (obligatory precaution): the calculator stops and refers. Whether it may show an indicative figure for the jurist is for the scholar to decide.

topic: Settlement (musalaha or dastgardan) for inability to pay
states: If unable to pay at once or it causes unbearable hardship, a jurist or his agent may transfer the khums to the person's liability at market value; it must then be repaid as able, instalments without delay; not allowed if one can pay at once.
issues: Settlement is with a jurist: recorded, never computed.

topic: Repaying a settled khums from next year's income
states: If the fifth (or its replacement) still exists and is unspent, it becomes next year's income; if it was lost or spent, the repayment is mu'nah. If unpaid, the fifth is not yet new income.
issues: Needs carry-over of settled debts and repayments.

topic: Paying one-fifth vs one-quarter
states: Paying a fifth from the item itself, from same-year income whose year passed, or from taxed money fully taxes the item. Paying from later years' income: a quarter fully taxes it; a fifth leaves a fifth of the item liable next year if it remains unused (worked example). Full taxing is optional.
issues: The one-quarter case needs carry-over of partially taxed items.

topic: Settled khums on working capital (example)
states: After settling a fifth, the taxed base is four-fifths; next year, last year's taxed base and the unpaid khums debt are deducted before new khums; settling a quarter makes the whole base taxed.
issues: Needs carry-over of the taxed base and settled debt.

topic: Settled khums on a shop (example)
states: Settling a fifth: four-fifths taxed; later rises owe nothing until the debt is paid from a later year's income, when a fifth of the shop becomes that year's income; settling a quarter makes it fully taxed.
issues: Needs carry-over of settled amounts.

topic: Minors and the insane
states: Maturity and sanity are not conditions: their unspent income is liable; the guardian pays, otherwise they do after maturity or recovery; also for mines, treasure, diving, mixed wealth.
issues: The calculator assesses one adult.

topic: Mahr, khul' payment and diyah
states: Not liable even after a year passes.

topic: Selling blood or an organ
states: Selling an organ whose loss is a bodily deficiency: liability problematic, observe precaution; selling blood: the price is income.

topic: Inheritance: conditions for exemption
states: Exempt even after a year if: (a) inherited under valid rules (ta'sib is a gain); (b) expected (unexpected from other than father or child: obligatory precaution to pay if above the year's expenses); (c) khums had not become due on it during the deceased's life; (d) the deceased did not owe khums.
issues: Already encoded in the 0.10.0 packs (sis-1771); note 'father or child' here vs 'father or son' in Tawdih 1771.

topic: Inherited property with unpaid khums
states: As Tawdih 1772, adding: a will to pay khums is executed from the whole estate even beyond one third.

topic: Doubt whether the deceased paid
states: If khums was due on it and one doubts payment, pay it by obligatory precaution (except the 589 exception).

topic: Unknown whether inherited property was liable
states: If unknown whether it was liable (e.g. could be mahr) or bought from taxed money: the heir need not pay.

topic: Endowing property bought from the year's income
states: Endowed before the year passes: exempt for founder and beneficiaries; beyond status, obligatory precaution on the excess.

topic: Income from a private endowment
states: As Tawdih 1775.

topic: Gift by bank transfer
states: For the recipient, as subsidies (620); for the giver, until withdrawn it is the giver's property but exempt if within status and not recoverable, or spent by the recipient before the giver's year end.
issues: Shetab-specific.

topic: Gift cards
states: Recipient: as subsidies; giver: as 622.

topic: Hajj and ziyarah costs
states: As Tawdih 1795.

topic: Hajj registration paid from income
states: Registration money for a later hajj or umrah owes khums at year end, unless the pilgrimage is already obligatory and settled on the person, registration is the only way, and there is no other money to pay its khums.

topic: Hajj contract for a later date
states: Khums on the value of the claim, unless the 628 exception applies.

topic: Hajj queue deposit discovered years later
states: Pay khums on the current bank balance; sale of the queue right is income of that year; a bought queue right: khums on the price paid.

topic: Tax is not khums
states: Tax paid cannot count as khums; customary tax paid from the year's income is mu'nah, even for past years' tax.

topic: Paying khums in kind or money
states: From the property itself or its money value; another kind of property needs a jurist's permission.

topic: Effect of paying from the item or other taxed money
states: Paying from the item: the rest is taxed; from other taxed money: the whole item is taxed.

topic: Paying khums on part of the property
states: Allowed for separable property; for one piece (part of a house or land) problematic without a jurist's permission.

topic: Overpaid khums by mistake
states: Cannot count it towards next year without a jurist; may reclaim from the recipient if it exists, or its replacement if the recipient knew.
